title: Adiabatic Computing Cores Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Adiabatic Computing Cores operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Adiabatic Computing Cores installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 51606 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where adiabatic drivers monitoring, core logistics redundancy, or slow clocks maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Adiabatic Computing Cores Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Adiabatic Computing Cores: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Adiabatic Computing Cores — cores recycling charge to approach zero energy.

Phase 1 — Prove (adiabatic drivers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (core logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (slow clocks): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (energy recovery): core hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and datacenters-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
